answer.rationale: Current situation: write path p99 latency is 5x target during peak settlement traffic. The release cannot be rolled back (compliance lock on security patch). Read replica routing (memory_b5) is mitigation for read load, not write latency. Regional failover (memory_b2) risks consistency during heavy writes and doesn't address root cause. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) would fail writes, violating primary objective. Adding capacity (memory_b3 model) directly addresses write saturation at peak load—headroom provisioning proved effective during promotional surge. This preserves the mandatory release, protects write throughput, and can be implemented as a standard experiment (gradual capacity addition) rather than emergency escalation, leaving options open if diagnosis reveals other factors.
